'''Mohammed Abouzaid''' ({{Langx|ar|محمد أبوزيد}}; born 1981) is a Moroccan mathematician working in [[symplectic topology]]. He is a professor at [[Stanford University]]. He obtained his PhD in 2007 at the [[University of Chicago]] under [[Paul Seidel]]'s supervision.

== Education and career ==
Mohammed Abouzaid was born in 1981.<ref>Mathematics People: "Abouzaid, Galatius, and Maulik Named Clay Research Fellows". ''[[Notices of the AMS]]'' v. 54 n. 7 p. 890 https://www.ams.org/notices/200707/tx070700890p.pdf</ref> In 2007, he received his PhD under the supervision of [[Paul Seidel]] from the [[University of Chicago]] with thesis ''Homological Mirror Symmetry for Toric Varieties''.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Mohammed Abouzaid |url=https://mathematics.stanford.edu/people/mohammed-abouzaid |access-date=2026-05-23 |website=Department of Mathematics, Stanford University}}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url=https://mathgenealogy.org/id.php?id=119150 | title=Mohammed Abouzaid - the Mathematics Genealogy Project }}</ref> As a postdoctoral researcher, he was a [[Clay Mathematics Institute]] Research Fellow from 2007 to 2012, concurrently, he was also a postdoctoral fellow at [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]]. From 2012 to 2013, he was a visiting professor at the [[Simons Center for Geometry and Physics]]. From 2012 to 2023, he was an associate professor at Columbia University.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Our team |url=https://schms.math.berkeley.edu/our-team/ |access-date=2026-05-23 |website=Simons Collaboration on Homological Mirror Symmetry |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.claymath.org/people/mohammed-abouzaid/ | title=Mohammed Abouzaid }}</ref> Since 2023 he has been Professor of Mathematics at [[Stanford University]].<ref name=":0" />

As of 2026, he supervised 7 PhD students.<ref>{{MathGenealogy|id=119150}}</ref>

== Awards and honors ==
Abouzaid was an invited speaker the [[International Congress of Mathematicians]] in 2014.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.mathunion.org/icm-plenary-and-invited-speakers | title=ICM Plenary and Invited Speakers &#124; International Mathematical Union (IMU) }}</ref> In 2017, he won the [[New Horizons in Mathematics Prize]] "For distinguishing cotangent bundles of exotic spheres, constructing the wrapped [[Fukaya category]] with Paul Seidel, and other decisive contributions to [[Symplectic geometry|symplectic topology]] and [[Reflection symmetry|mirror symmetry]]."<ref name="bkf">{{cite web | url=https://breakthroughprize.org/Laureates/3/L3805 | title=Breakthrough Prize – Mathematics Breakthrough Prize Laureates – Mohammed Abouzaid }}</ref> In 2018 he became a fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]].<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.math.columbia.edu/2017/11/02/congratulations-to-dr-abouzaid/ | title=Department of Mathematics at Columbia University - CONGRATULATIONS to Professor Abouzaid! }}</ref>
